title: Longest strictly increasing subsequence
summary: Pick people from a line, keeping their order, to build the longest staircase of rising heights.
goal: Find how many people the tallest staircase can have

mapping.story: Longest staircase ending with this person
Smallest top for each staircase length

examples.label: All the same height
examples.explanation: Equal heights are not rising, so each staircase has one person.

ladder.name: Try every selection
ladder.idea: Check every subset of people, in line order, for strictly rising heights, and keep the largest.

ladder.name: Longest staircase ending with each person
ladder.idea: For each person, look at everyone before them who is shorter and extend the longest staircase that ends there.
ladder.insight: A staircase ending with person i is a staircase ending with some shorter person before them, plus person i. Writing those lengths down makes each one a single scan.

ladder.name: Keep the smallest top for each length
ladder.idea: Keep, for each staircase length, the smallest possible top height. Each person replaces the first top that is at least their height, found by binary search, or extends the longest staircase.
ladder.insight: For staircases of the same length, a lower top is always at least as good for extending. Those smallest tops are sorted, so each person's place is found by binary search.

transfer.problem: Stack boxes by height and width so each box is strictly smaller than the one below it; maximise the number of boxes, keeping a given order.
transfer.explanation: It is a longest increasing subsequence under a stricter comparison: best chain ending with each box.

selfCheck: Keeps the original order of the line.
Replaces the first top that is not smaller than the new height.
Returns 1 for a line of equal heights.
